text:
kari: Noticed a weird edge: console impersonation requests sometimes lose the console-specified project when routed through our api-gateway, ends up charging the SA owner org. Quick repro below.
kari: Repro: Console > Run sample > Impersonate sa-data-pipeline@acme > pick project=proj-ops > send -> dashboard shows charge on org-acme.
kari: Raw forwarded headers from gateway trace: `Authorization: Bearer ...; X-Impersonate: sa-data-pipeline; X-Console-Project: proj-ops; X-Org: org-acme`
devin: Gateway log shows header rewrite for security: we normalize incoming headers and explicitly drop any unexpected X-* unless allowlist set. It looks like X-Console-Project wasn't in allowlist for the impersonation route.
hema: Oh. We added stricter header hygiene for the gateway last quarter to avoid header injection. We probably missed adding the console impersonation flow to the whitelist.
billing-bot: alert: small uptick in org billing anomalies detected 2026-03-22T08:00Z - correlate with impersonation routes.
karI: (typo) kari: ops: can we add a small telemetry field to the quota meter showing which source produced effective_project: token_claim / header / sa_owner? That would make triage trivial.
devin: Yes, add enum `effective_project_source` to quota event. I can add it in router PR.
hema: Meanwhile to reduce customer impact we should fallback to reading `X-Console-Project` from the original inbound request before gateway normalization and inject into the token payload at mint time (for console-origin ephemeral tokens). That avoids depending on header passthrough downstream.
devin: That is safer. Two parallel fixes: A) quick gateway allowlist change to keep X-Console-Project for impersonation flows (fast rollbackable), B) keygen service attach `effective_project` claim on mint, validated against membership (longer term). Put both behind feature flags.
ops-bot: deploy: canary gateway v2.14 tonight at 23:00 PDT. Tag: authz:impersonation-gateway-fix.
billing-bot: To billing: please run db query for requests labelled impersonation where charge_target=org-acme in last 48h and post a short sample set. We'll need to scope credits.
hema: Security note: when attaching project claim at mint, enforce that user creating the key is member of the chosen project. Logging/audit event must include who minted and what project was set.
devin: Also add a telemetry flag `ui_warning_shown` for console flows if selected SA has no project binding and router would have charged org. Console should show a small inline banner.
kari: For UX: small banner "This request will be billed to org-acme because sa-data-pipeline has no default project. Set a default project on the service account to bill requests to a project." Link to docs. Keeps support noise down.
hema: Timeline: I'll open PR for keygen change (unit tests + membership check). Devin, can you do gateway allowlist PR? We'll gate keygen change behind `authz:mint-project-claim`.
devin: Yep. I will also add router telemetry change to include `effective_project_source`. Then we can run a canary for 24h and monitor `billing_charge_via` distribution.
billing-bot: Once we have telemetry we can quantify impact and propose customer credits. Please escalate if >0.2% of requests in production show org-charge during canary.
kari: Thanks. Can you ping #support with repro steps and short customer-facing explanation? I'll include the banner copy and docs link.
ops-bot: reminder: include rollback playbook in PR description and add runbook for SRE.
hema: I'll post PR links here when ready. ETA: 3h for gateway PR, 6h for keygen and router telemetry.
devin: I'll review and land the gateway change quickly.
kari: Appreciate the fast turnaround :thumbsup:
